knowledge_answers.rationale: A batter out of ground is Run out when the wicket at that ground is fairly broken, subject to the stated exceptions.
An appeal may follow Dead ball; it must be made before the bowler begins the run-up or action for the next delivery and before Time at innings close.
Absence creates or carries unserved Penalty time subject to the Law's caps and exceptions; the player may not bowl until all of that time has been served.
The first contravention creates a team-wide warning; a later contravention by any player of that team is a repeat; five Penalty runs are awarded to the opponents and the incident is reported.

The MCC baseline requires agreed result criteria where its ordinary win provisions do not decide the match; the concrete reduced-overs formula belongs to the match's versioned playing conditions; commentary cannot replace that governing local instrument.

derivation.rule_text: Multiply the fours count by 4, multiply the sixes count by 6, then add the products.
Multiply runs by 100, divide by balls faced, and round half up to two decimals.
Add the fours count and sixes count to obtain the number of boundary-scoring events.
Multiply conceded runs by 6, divide by legal balls, and round half up to two decimals.
Add the fours count and sixes count to obtain the number of boundary-scoring events.
